chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer, and he who plunders a valuable spoil does not plunder it while he is a believer.' Ibn Sinan said: I said to Abu al-Jarud, 'What is a valuable spoil?' He said, 'Similar to what Hatim did when he said: Whoever takes something, it is his.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Prophet says the fornicator is not a believer while committing the sin?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of 'temporary suspension of faith' (Tawaqquf al-Iman), distinguishing between the permanent loss of faith (Kufr) and the temporary diminution of Iman during the commission of major sins. The specific mention of 'plundering a valuable spoil' (Nuhbat Dhat Sharaf) is contextualized by the companion Ibn Sinan’s inquiry, which links the concept to the pre-Islamic ethos of absolute possession exemplified by Hatim al-Attar, highlighting a transition in how value and ownership were understood. This hadith is central to the debate between the Shia and Khawarij regarding whether major sins constitute disbelief or merely a deficiency in faith.
